To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TCMH can be demonstrated in vitro by LMCT in hypernephromatous patients; the antigenicity of tumor cells is a feature of the tumor; the capacity of hypernephrormatous patients to develop a TCMH is not impaired; and the development of TCMI may be dependent on the antigenicity, less on the capacity of the immune response.
TCMH is found in patients with hypernephroma and is associated with tumor elimination.
the antigenicity of renal tumors is a feature of their malignant behavior, and that tumor-specific cell-mediated immunity is a factor in tumor elimination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible immunotherapeutic approach to hypernephroma.
the question of whether TCMH is of prognostic significance for the clinical course of renal carcinoma.
the development of an in vitro test for the detection of TCMH, and with the clinical application of the method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LMCT test is of prognostic significance in patients with renal carcinoma, and the antigenicity of renal carcinoma may be of importance for the clinical course of the disease.
the development of TCMh is a favorable prognostic factor, and the absence of TCMH an adverse one.
the presence of a cell-mediated immune reactivity against autologous or allogeneic hypernephroma is a good prognostic factor for tumor elimination and long-term survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TCMH may be a prognostically important factor in the management of renal tumors.
the antigenic properties of the renal tumor may be of great importance for the prognosis of hypernephromas.
the LMCT technique may be useful in the clinical evaluation of renal tumors, and that the technique may be of value in the evaluation of tumor elimination in other types of malignant disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antigenicity of renal cell carcinoma is high and that the tumor-specific cell-mediated immune response can be detected in vivo by the LMCT.

TCMH can be detected in hypernephroma, that the antigenicity is found in autogenous as well as allogenous tumor tissue and fetal kidney tissue and that the antigenicity of small noninvasive tumors is high, whereas tumors with a tendency to early dispersion show a lower antigenicity.
the antigenicity of a tumor is of importance for its immunogenicity and that TCMH may be of importance for tumor elimination.
